name: Adam's apple enhancement

lead: Adam's apple enhancement enlarges the bump at the front of the neck, which is usually more pronounced in men, to give a more masculine neckline. The change is directly visible in the neck profile.

A surgeon adds volume over the thyroid cartilage, with a custom implant or cartilage work. It appears in the literature mainly as part of facial masculinization surgery for transmasculine patients, alongside mandible angle and chin procedures. One 2025 report followed six patients who received personalized PEEK implants planned from scans.

paras: It is done as a surgical procedure, often alongside other facial masculinization work such as jaw and chin changes. Results are visible once the surgical swelling settles.
It is surgery near the larynx, so complications are possible. The published series is small (six patients), so complication rates are not established.

angle.text: Surgical enlargement of the Adam's apple adds a visible prominence at the front of the neck for a more masculine profile. It is described mainly as part of facial masculinization for transmasculine patients, in small case series.

lead: Adam's apple enhancement, sometimes called laryngeal or tracheal augmentation, is a surgical procedure that enlarges the visible laryngeal prominence at the front of the neck, which is typically more pronounced in men. [1] It is described in the medical literature mainly as one component of facial masculinization surgery for transmasculine patients, alongside mandible angle and chin procedures. [2]

Published evidence is limited to small surgical series; one 2025 report followed six transmasculine patients who received personalized PEEK implants planned with virtual surgical planning. [2] Within looksmaxxing communities the topic appears as a hardmaxxing option for a more masculine neck, though no community-specific studies were found.

paras: The Adam's apple is the protrusion formed by the angle of the thyroid cartilage around the larynx. Everyone with typical anatomy has one, but it is usually more visible in men, because testosterone-driven laryngeal growth in puberty moves the prominence forward. [1]

In the literature found, augmentation is grouped under facial masculinization surgery for transmasculine patients, with mandible angle, chin and tracheal augmentation. [2] A 2025 study described patient-specific PEEK implants created from preoperative scans using virtual surgical planning. [2] The Wikipedia article on the laryngeal prominence notes that some transgender men choose augmentation, while testosterone therapy can also enlarge the larynx and is described as much more common than surgery. [1]

Evidence is limited. A 2025 study in the Journal of Craniofacial Surgery assessed outcomes and complications in six transmasculine patients who had facial masculinization with PEEK implants after virtual surgical planning; tracheal augmentation was among the procedure types discussed. [2] No controlled trials were found, and no studies of augmentation for cosmetic purposes in cisgender men were found.
The procedure is discussed as a possible way to add masculine neck definition. No forum material was cited for this article.
